content: 1. Carbamazepine reduces the levels of levonorgestrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzymes, which accelerates its metabolism. This interaction may compromise the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Alternative contraceptive methods should be considered. 2. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels of carbamazepine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may enhance carbamazepine's effects, necessitating close monitoring or the use of alternative drugs. 3. Cefaclor, cefdinir, cefixime, cefotaxime, cefpodoxime, ceftazidime, ceftibuten, cefuroxime, and cephalexin may reduce the levels of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This effect applies only to oral forms of hormonal contraceptives and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Cenobamate decreases the levels of both levonorgestrel and ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Women using cenobamate should be advised to use additional or alternative non-hormonal contraceptive methods. 5. Ceritinib increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. 6. Chloramphenicol reduces the levels of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral contraceptives and poses a low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitoring is recommended. 7. Cimetidine increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Ciprofloxacin reduces the levels of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This effect applies only to oral contraceptives and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitoring is recommended. 9. Clarithromycin reduces the levels of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. Ethinyl estradiol may also increase clarithromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 10. Clindamycin reduces the levels of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral contraceptives and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitoring is recommended. 11. Clobazam reduces the levels of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Clobazam is a weak CYP3A4 inducer, and its concurrent use may diminish the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives. Additional non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 12. Clomipramine levels may be increased by ethinyl estradiol due to inhibition of CYP1A2 metabolism. This interaction may lead to increased serum concentrations of clomipramine and potential adverse effects. Monitoring is recommended. 13. Conivaptan increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 14. Crofelermer increases the levels of levonorgestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the gut. This effect is unlikely to occur systemically due to minimal absorption. Monitoring is recommended. 15. Cyclophosphamide increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 16. Cyclosporine levels may be increased by ethinyl estradiol due to inhibition of its metabolism. Combined oral contraceptives containing ethinyl estradiol may increase plasma concentrations of cyclosporine. Monitoring is recommended. 17. Dabrafenib reduces the levels of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative contraceptive methods should be considered. 18. Dalteparin may reduce the effects of levonorgestrel due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction increases the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Alternative drugs should be considered. 19. Danazol increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 20. Dexamethasone reduces the levels of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative contraceptive methods are recommended. 21. Diazepam levels may be increased by ethinyl estradiol due to inhibition of benzodiazepine clearance via oxidative metabolism. This interaction may lead to increased serum concentrations of diazepam. Monitoring is recommended. 22. Dicloxacillin reduces the levels of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral contraceptives and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitoring is recommended. 23. Doxepin levels may be increased by ethinyl estradiol due to inhibition of oxidative metabolism. This interaction may lead to increased serum concentrations of doxepin and potential adverse effects. Monitoring is recommended. 24. Doxycycline reduces the levels of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral contraceptives and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Monitoring is recommended. 25. Drospirenone increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 26. Duloxetine levels may be increased by ethinyl estradiol due to inhibition of CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 27. Efavirenz reduces the levels of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative contraceptive methods are recommended. 28. Elafibranor reduces the levels of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Women should switch to effective non-hormonal contraceptives or add a barrier method during elafibranor treatment and for at least three weeks after the last dose. 29. Elagolix reduces the levels of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Women should use non-hormonal contraceptives during elagolix treatment and for one week after discontinuation. 30. Eltrombopag levels may be increased by ethinyl estradiol due to inhibition of CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 31. Elvitegravir reduces the levels of ethinyl estradiol by an unknown mechanism. Alternative drugs should be considered.
